nonvacuity: scratch/Check.lean compiles an explicit UnitExperiment on Fin 2 with probability 1/2 each on (true,false) and (false,true), zero elsewhere, both marginals 1/2, and one treated unit on every supported assignment. Outcomes and prediction arrays can be arbitrary real vectors/functions; e.g. y1=(1,2), y0=(0,0), f=0. No independence or zero-covariance premise is imposed here.

The 90-element allocation space is nonempty, normalized, and has treatment probabilities 1/2 on clusters 0-3 and 1/3 on clusters 4-9. Both observed-outcome blocks have two distinct covariate values and no nonzero weak separating direction, so their logistic likelihoods have unique finite maximizers. Independent 60-digit Decimal calculations give block-1 coefficients (1.0843222951194215,0.2280259453080925), block-2 coefficients (-1.1201075519520951,0.5657585557648923), ATE SD 0.247091750594593 and variance-estimator SD 0.0125667023899652. These are numerical corroboration, not a formal interval proof; existence and all moments are conclusions, not assumed premises.

The three equally likely assignments treat exactly one of three units. Treatment/control marginals are 1/3 and 2/3; the (intercept,i) real OLS matrix has full rank. Exact Fraction calculations verify both OLS normal equations for every fitted row, residual estimates (1/4,1,1/4), treatment-fit covariances (1/6,0,1/6), and expectation 1/2 against ATE 1. Revision 2 only clarifies the Challenge docstring: it explicitly refutes the reading that estate() with HT=TRUE remains unbiased when covariates X are supplied. The finite experiment, OLS interpretation, estimators, and numerical conclusions remain as in the blind reading; the new wording adds no mathematical premise.

The compiled two-unit UnitExperiment supplies positive marginals for every universal clause. Fixed predictions give the fixed-prediction branch; arbitrary covariates, including K=0, give a well-defined real Euclidean OLS projection. Under y1=y0=(1,2), the observed vector and its OLS fit are fixed, satisfying the sharp-null and zero-covariance cases. The separate three-unit example has bias -1/2 by exact arithmetic.

The stated three-point/two-unit real design (00,01,11), weights 1/3, has treatment marginals (1/3,2/3), positive control marginals, disagreement 1/3, and positive same-arm off-diagonal joints 1/3. Probability axioms, marginals and directed joints are checked in Lean. Exact Fraction arithmetic gives p10(0,1)=0, p10(1,0)=1/3, E[printedVariance(1,1)]=23/8 < 27/8=Var(HT(1,1))=Var(generalized(1,1,0)); the missing term is not a zero denominator artifact.

The four equally likely allocations 000,011,101,110 have all marginals 1/2. Exact enumeration verifies every focal/input joint cell is 1/4. The fit Y1+Y2-2*Y1*Y2 equals the focal treatment indicator, so its covariance with that indicator is 1/4. Lean independently checks probability axioms, positive marginals and the covariance value.

The table has exactly 90 positive-probability allocations. Exact Fraction enumeration verifies every FE denominator is positive, with minimum 2710/993, and derives the opposite-block OLS residual vector used in the theorem. It gives FE expectation approximately -0.013987426269439, outside the printed -0.012 rounding interval, and Linear variance 38307/634880, approximately 0.06033738659. Either mismatch suffices to negate the selected printed conjunction. Both logistic likelihoods are full rank and nonseparated, so their uniqueness conjuncts do not manufacture the refutation.

The compiled two-unit UnitExperiment has normalized nonnegative weights and both marginals 1/2. Taking y1=(1,2), y0=(0,0) gives HT values 1 and 2 on the two supported assignments, expectation 3/2 equal to the actual ATE. Both total estimators and all masking denominators are well-defined.

For clause (a), the compiled two-unit law has n=1, N=2, both marginals 1/2 and exactly one treated unit on every supported assignment. For (b), the compiled ClusterExperiment with U=C=Fin 2, identity partition and that assignment law has M=2,m=1 and satisfies the added condition. For (c), the explicit four-unit clusters (0),(1),(2,3) give realized treatment counts 1,1,2 and positive control counts; exact arithmetic gives differences in means (2/3,2/3,-1), expectation 1/9, versus HT expectation and ATE 0. Independent fair assignments of two singleton clusters show the added fixed-cluster-count premise is genuinely stronger than uniform marginals.

The compiled two-unit law and any deterministic prediction vector g, for example (3,4), satisfy the zero-covariance premise with both marginals 1/2. Sharp-null potential outcomes also give assignment-invariant observed outcomes. Hence the antecedent does not assume unbiasedness, and the unconditional adjustment identity permits arbitrary assignment-dependent predictions.

The compiled two-unit law instantiates the universal block with arbitrary real affine constants. The supported failure witness has one unit, three equally likely sample points, treatment only at point 2, hence p1=1/3 and p0=2/3. At point 2 with b0=1,b1=-1 and original outcomes zero, transformed HT is 3 while b1 times original HT is 0. No realized-arm-size division occurs.

The compiled identity-partition two-cluster experiment is nonempty, surjective, has both marginals 1/2 and positive disagreement (indeed 1), meeting the cluster antecedent. The asymmetric three-point/two-cluster design additionally satisfies positive disagreement while p10(0,1)=0; it can be encoded on all four binary allocations by assigning weight zero to 10. The full, split and off-diagonal covariance formulas still agree because each zero cross joint contributes -Xc*Zd. Fixed r and arbitrary real potential outcomes instantiate the variance block without any zero denominator.
